title: Entity growth batch 04 — group E
notes: Breadth-first candidate group for Issue #203. Casa is modeled with a hybrid custody/key boundary because Casa holds one recovery key that cannot independently move funds. Canonical publication prohibited until validation and manual review complete.

entities.summary: Open-source Bitcoin desktop wallet and node interface focused on hardware-wallet and multisignature setups, with Bitcoin Core and Electrum backends.
entities.notes: Official project documentation describes Specter Desktop primarily as a watch-only Bitcoin Core/Electrum wallet GUI whose signing keys live on user-controlled hardware/signing devices; an optional hot-wallet mode exists but is not the normal security boundary. The repository remains actively maintained in August 2026. Initial launch date remains unresolved.

entities.summary: Non-custodial multisignature Bitcoin and Ethereum vault service in which users control the signing quorum while Casa holds one emergency recovery key that cannot move funds by itself.

system_components.custody_note: Held by the user on the mobile device.
One or more user-controlled hardware-wallet keys participate in the multisig quorum.
Casa holds one recovery key, but that key alone cannot move funds or satisfy the multisig quorum.

entities.notes: Casa explicitly calls the vault non-custodial because Casa never holds enough keys to move funds. WLR still records `custody_model=hybrid` to preserve the material provider-held recovery-key component rather than flattening the architecture into a pure user-only key model.

entities.summary: Open-source hardware wallet ecosystem with device-held offline private keys and current companion software.
entities.notes: Current first-party KeepKey material says the hardware wallet has secured crypto since 2014, stores private keys on the device, is currently in stock and receives free firmware updates for life. Year precision only.

entities.summary: Open-source smart-card hardware wallet using an EAL6+ secure element to keep user private keys inside the card.
entities.notes: Current first-party Satochip product and quick-start material establishes an actively sold self-custody hardware wallet whose private keys remain in an EAL6+ secure element. Initial launch date remains unresolved.

entities.summary: Hardware-wallet ecosystem whose Prokey Optimum device keeps private keys offline and uses a web-based companion wallet interface.
entities.notes: Prokey's first-party launch post dated 2020-07-02 explicitly announces the launch of the first product in its hardware-wallet lineup, Prokey Optimum. The current product page continues to offer the device for sale.

products.summary: Actively maintained Specter Desktop Bitcoin wallet GUI for hardware-wallet, multisig and Bitcoin Core/Electrum workflows.
products.notes: Support status is `supported` because the official repository contains current August 2026 wallet, dependency and security-related maintenance commits. This does not imply Specter normally holds the user's signing keys.

products.summary: Casa Standard 2-of-3 multisig vault using a user mobile key, a user hardware key and a Casa-held recovery key, where any two signatures are required.
products.notes: Selected vault product rather than treating Casa's advisory/service layer as a wallet. Casa holds only one of three keys and cannot move funds unilaterally.

products.summary: Current KeepKey hardware wallet with offline device-held private keys and open-source firmware/hardware design.
products.notes: Current first-party pages say the device is in stock and promise free firmware updates for life; WLR therefore records current sale and support explicitly.

products.summary: Satochip smart-card hardware wallet using an EAL6+ secure element and current desktop/mobile integrations.
products.notes: Current first-party product page offers Satochip for purchase and states private keys cannot be extracted from the secure chip. Support status remains conservative `unknown` rather than inferring a formal maintenance commitment from current documentation alone.

products.summary: Prokey Optimum hardware wallet with offline device-held private keys and a web-based wallet interface.
products.notes: First-party launch article explicitly launches Prokey Optimum on 2020-07-02; the current product page offers it for purchase. Support status remains conservative `unknown`.
